title: Verifier feedback raised both correct and incorrect model verdicts
summary: On 32 software verification tasks, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B averaged 22.0 correct verdicts with verifier feedback versus 12.7 without it. Incorrect verdicts also rose from one to seven. A deterministic validation baseline returned 26 correct verdicts and left six unresolved.
organization: The University of Manchester; University of Rajshahi; Varendra University

source_review.scope: §§III–IV, E3 frozen-subset design, Figure 3 and interpretation limits

evidence.tested: The fixed assertion set was evaluated with and without feedback for three seeds. Correct, incorrect and unresolved decisions were counted separately.
evidence.unknown: The subset was small and selected from one verification benchmark. The deterministic baseline included an additional validation step and is not an equivalent raw-feedback condition.
evidence.ai_role: The trained coding model interpreted formal-verification evidence, allowing a direct comparison of verdicts under controlled feedback conditions.
